title: Handle duplicate source timestamps and verify dense selection completeness
description: Dense extraction worker discovered a pre-existing reproducible MJPEG Invalid pts failure with duplicate source PTS and replaced its original generated fixture instead of fixing the failure. Complete the plan by repairing it with real-media regression. Own src/media.js and test/dense-extraction.test.js plus test/vfr-extraction.test.js only if needed. Preserve last-frame-at-or-before semantics; duplicate-PTS source frames should resolve deterministically to last decoded at equal PTS. Rebase encoded output timestamps after selecting source frames (e.g. setpts=N) without rebasing source comparison/showinfo. Verify dense batch completion cannot incorrectly confirm a guessed earlier PTS when -frames:v guesses.length stops before an unlisted eligible source frame; reproduce and repair if real. Preserve source manifest times, sparse fallbacks, cancellation, crop/SAR dimensions. No CLI/plan/changes/seek/process/output/sheets/docs edits. Keep new tests behavioral, avoid tautologies.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate-PTS real video succeeds for sparse and dense extraction with deterministic last-at/before pixel evidence; batch verification covers complete requested span; VFR/seek/dense tests pass.
notes:
Implemented (parent closes). Files: src/media.js, test/dense-extraction.test.js (vfr test untouched).
Repro: mkv with pairs of frames sharing each pts (libx264 B-frames, -bf 0 too) failed frame and inspect with MJPEG 'Invalid pts (0) <= last (0)'.
Fix: filters() starts with setpts=N/TB and both encodes use -enc_time_base:v 1, so encoded frames are numbered by whole seconds; select/trim/showinfo stay before it on source pts. Per-time -update keeps the last kept frame = last decoded at equal pts. Chunks select every frame at a guessed pts and map each time to encoded.lastIndexOf(shown pts). Dropped -frames:v guesses.length: decode now runs to trim end, so showinfo sees every frame <= the last time (completeness by construction; extra files from unlisted frames are added to produced; the work dir is removed whole anyway).
-frames:v false-confirm check: not reproducible. Old code with a faked ffprobe hiding the frame shown at the chunk's last time (CFR no-B 360p and 1080p bf3, 16 runs) and an old-structure mutant on duplicates (10 runs) always gave correct frames: frames in flight still reached showinfo. Now safe by construction.
Evidence: pre-change vs new byte-identical (frames, sheets, manifests) on test.mov: inspect 0-10s@10, overlapping cropped windows@30, frame 0.266/7.125/7.25, overview. New tests: duplicate-pts case in the main dense matrix (chunked, no per-time fallback, pixel-checked vs independent origin decode, every time shows the second of its pair, byte-equal to the sparse 'frame' path); a faked listing missing a frame -> only that time falls back and pixels are correct. Encode-count bound generalized (counted from files written by a logging wrapper, since -frames:v is gone). Mutations: no setpts -> Invalid pts; indexOf (first dup) -> pixel fail; verifying against the listing -> unlisted test fails. Full suite 93/93. Quick 1080p timing old vs new comparable (load ~8).
Risks: earlier duplicates at a shown pts are also JPEG-encoded (one extra per duplicate). A time before the first frame (window 0, -frames:v 1) shows the first decoded frame, not the last of a duplicated first pts. If ffmpeg's best-effort pts falls back to dts on heavily faulty pts, chunks fail verification and use the per-time path (correct but slower).
close_reason: Reviewed source selection before encoder timestamp renumbering, duplicate-PTS last-decoded mapping and full-span batch verification. Independent pixel/hidden-packet regressions and full suite 93/93 pass; public timeline contract unchanged.

title: Enforce change-analysis budget on origin retries
description: During verification of agvid-aoh.7, worker disclosed that analysis budget checks nominal scan span but origin retries can decode arbitrarily more video. Enforce budget before each slow/origin fallback in detectChanges; if range.end-info.start exceeds settings.budget, fail before spawning that fallback with narrow/raise guidance. Track successful actual scan start/span in detection.scan instead of reporting nominal seek start for an origin retry. Budget is source-span limit, not wall-clock or cumulative retries; document later. Also check explicitly provided start>=end before ffprobe (source-independent contradiction). Own changes.js/plan.js and test/changes-workflow.test.js only. Regression must use real sparse long timestamp video or instrumented FFmpeg with real media to prove denied origin fallback does not start. Preserve within-budget origin recovery, seek behavior, progress, candidates and temporal selection.
acceptance_criteria: Every actual origin fallback obeys configured source-span budget before spawn; successful manifest reports actual decoded span; contradictory explicit ranges fail before probing; regression and targeted seek tests pass.
notes: Implemented (Opus 5.5). plan.js: parseOptions rejects explicit --start>=--end before ffprobe (all commands); new exported checkBudget(from,end,budget,origin) shared by planRun and detectChanges; scanSpan removed (inlined). changes.js: before any slow attempt when attempt 0 was a seek, checkBudget(info.start, range.end) inside the Promise executor -> rejects before spawning FFmpeg, message 'input seeking found no frame at the range start, so it is decoded from the video start ... narrow it with --end or raise --analysis-budget'. Successful attempt returns actual from; detection.scan={from,to,seconds,budget} reflects it; progress from/seconds/candidates reset per attempt; settings.scan no longer used. Evidence: real sparse FLV w/ x264 B-frames (frames at 0,1,39s) misses on -ss 20 (bd before fix reported scan.from 20 while decoding from 0). Test 'a fallback to the video start ... must fit the budget before it starts': budget 25 fails, no output dir, only -ss 20 scans spawned; budget 40 runs origin scan, scan {from:0,to:40,seconds:40}, frames [20,39] gray/white pixel-checked. Mutations (disable check / nominal from / drop start>=end check) each fail a test. Checks: full suite node --test test/*.test.js 92/92 pass. Risk: fixture relies on FFmpeg FLV demuxer seek miss with B-frames (verified on local FFmpeg); budget is per-attempt source span, not cumulative across retries — docs (agvid-aoh.8).
close_reason: Reviewed resumed Opus implementation: budget checked before origin retries, actual successful span reported, contradictory ranges rejected pre-probe. Real sparse FLV regression plus seek/workflow and full suite (92/92) passed.

description: Own changes module, planning/argument module and src/cli.js integration plus new test/changes-workflow.test.js only. Validate source-independent inputs before ffprobe. Acquire/check output before expensive changes detection and ensure release on error/cancel. Add explicit processing-duration budget (suggest --analysis-budget seconds, default 300s) that rejects oversized scan pre-FFmpeg with start/end/override guidance; include actual origin decode cost for TS if needed. Add low-noise timed stderr scan progress leaving stdout JSON clean. Keep RGB metric/reference/min-gap semantics. Select strong events across time buckets when max truncates, retain late quieter events, bounded candidate storage and precise pts. Include candidates/truncated in stdout JSON and selection/budget metadata manifest. Measure detector thread flags independently; preserve frame pairing/memory bounds and origin retry.
acceptance_criteria: Long scan budget and output/arg failures occur before expensive work; progress stderr; truncated results cover whole timeline incl quieter late events; manifest and stdout expose loss; real-video validation passes.
notes:
Impl (Opus subagent), not closed; parent verifies. Files: src/plan.js, src/changes.js, src/cli.js (HELP untouched; doc worker must add --analysis-budget, progress, selection, early output claim), test/changes-workflow.test.js (new), test/cli.test.js (only '--max caps...240 frames' tie expectation: last kept 23.9 -> 25.9, fromSlices 239; intentional).

Events/scores identical (max 239) on both clips. Rejected: +filter_threads 1, decoder -threads 4/8 (no gain). Output -threads:v 1 also single-threaded the filter graph; removed.
Tests: changes-workflow 4/4 (quiet late change kept over crowding strong ones with pixel check; arg/budget/TS/occupied-output fail with zero ffprobe/scan calls; progress stderr + SIGTERM cleanup with FFmpeg pids gone; inspect range). title: Batch dense inspect decoding and deduplicate overlapping extraction
description: Own media/extraction module and new test/dense-extraction.test.js only. Use established extractFrames API to batch dense inspect windows (and near events only if safe) in one decode per dense group, choose final eligible source frame before JPEG encoding, reuse exact shared times across overlapping windows while preserving separate frame entries/sheets. Keep sparse seeking for overview/widely spaced frame calls and fallback for tricky containers/sparse VFR. Avoid fps resampling selecting later frames. Bounded memory, process/output count, cancellation. Verify against independent per-time origin decode at CFR/VFR boundaries, sparse holds, delayed starts, rotation/crop/TS; manifests remain requested-time evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Dense inspect substantially faster without changed temporal evidence; no repeated JPEG encode for intermediate candidates; overlap shares decode/image work; meaningful pixel comparisons and seek suite pass.
notes:
Implemented (not closed; parent verifies). Files: src/media.js, test/dense-extraction.test.js.
Design: inspect only. Unique sorted times; consecutive gaps <=1s form dense groups, split into chunks >=1s span (unsplit when the group's last time decodes from origin: TS/near start). Per chunk: ffprobe demux-only packet listing guesses the pts shown at each time; one ffmpeg decode (same seek/origin rule as extract) with trim,showinfo,select=eq(pts,...),showinfo,crop/scale -> image2 sequence, -frames:v = guesses. Each time is verified against showinfo of every decoded frame (last decoded pts <= time); unverified times, failed chunks, listings with N/A pts (AVI) and sparse times use the unchanged per-time extract (passthrough + bounded decoder threads kept). Equal times / times sharing a shown frame are encoded once and copied; manifest entries/files/sheets stay separate. No fps filter. Cancellation rethrown.
Evidence: outputs byte-identical to pre-change per-time path on bundled test.mov (inspect 8/30/100/225 frames, overlapping windows) and 1080p60 GOP250 clip (60, 24 frames). Tests (3, real videos): independent origin-decode pixel comparison at CFR B-frames, VFR test.mov, sparse holds mkv, delayed-start MP4 edit list, MPEG-TS, rotation+crop, AVI fallback; byte equality vs frame command; encode count <= distinct+chunks-1; overlap 16 entries/10 encodes/2 sheets; SIGTERM -> 143, ffmpeg dead, output removed. Mutations (later frame, encode all candidates, no copies) each fail tests. Full suite 92/92.
Bench median of 5 (load 5-21, direction only) old->new: bundled inspect8 0.78->0.78, bundled 0-10s@10 3.97->1.83, 1080p inspect8 1.85->0.86, 1080p 0-10s@10 13.3->4.2, 1080p 2s@30 11.4->2.0, 1080p 3 windows@8 3.8->1.6. CHUNK_SPAN 0.5/0.25 slower on long GOP.
Risks: frame held across a chunk boundary is encoded once per chunk; AVI-like containers get one ffprobe listing then per-time; pre-existing: streams with duplicate pts make MJPEG fail (per-time path too).
close_reason: Reviewed resumed Opus implementation and evidence: dense inspect chunks encode selected source PTS, overlap/time dedup and checked fallbacks. Independent pixel tests across CFR/VFR/TS/delayed start/crop/rotation/AVI plus cancellation pass; 92/92 full suite. Duplicate-PTS defect is separately gated follow-up.

title: Fix VFR extraction synchronization and measure workload-specific thread tuning
description: Own media/extraction module and new test/vfr-extraction.test.js only. Fix default FFmpeg synchronization dropping latest eligible VFR frame (bundled test.mov at 7.125s) with explicit passthrough. Add meaningful independently decoded pixel evidence for last frame at/before time. Preserve sparse/VFR, nonzero/delayed starts, B frames, TS, SAR/rotation/crop, exact requested manifest times. Benchmark decoder/filter/MJPEG thread flags for sparse extraction and avoid oversubscription; never apply universal limits to detection. Simplify duplicate seek attempts only with behavior evidence; retain origin fallback. Coordinate no media edits outside ownership.
acceptance_criteria: Independent real-video VFR regression and full existing seek suite pass; thread policy chosen from measurements and recorded in issue.
notes:
Implementation done (not closed; parent verifies). Files: src/media.js, test/vfr-extraction.test.js. src/seek.js unchanged (shared attempts/seekArgs/trimEnd semantics kept for changes.js).

VFR fix: extract() adds '-fps_mode passthrough' (default CFR sync at r_frame_rate 60 dropped a kept VFR frame sharing an output tick). Evidence, test.mov --width 1280, mean abs gray diff on pixels distinguishing neighbor frames (independent from-origin pts-selected decode):
- 7.125 (want 7.100): old closest 7.083 (3.0 vs 49.8); new 7.100 (4.3 vs 47.1)
- 0.266 (want 0.100): old 0.083; new 0.100
- 7.225/7.25/7.275 (want 7.2167): old 7.200; new 7.2167
Baseline diff (benchmark/baseline-src vs new): manifests identical; overview48 1 frame (0.266), inspect 6.5-8@20fps 3 frames (7.125/7.225/7.275), frame at 7.125/7.25 changed, all to the correct frame; 1080p CFR testsrc2 frames byte-identical.
Test: test/vfr-extraction.test.js (times 0.266, 7.125, 7.25) fails without passthrough, passes with. vfr + seek.test.js: 12/12 pass.

Thread policy (chosen): decoder '-threads floor(cores/jobs)' as input option when jobs=min(times,cores,8)>1; jobs=1 keeps FFmpeg auto. Encoder stays -threads:v 1; filter_threads default. Only extractFrames; detection untouched.
Trials (16 cores, interleaved, median s, isolated /tmp copy; host load avg 25-42 from concurrent agents, so treat as directional; final benchmark should verify):
5 runs cur vs adaptive: bundled frame1 .39/.39, frame5 .60/.54, overview12 1.04/.91, overview48 2.85/2.33, inspect8 .92/.77; short1080p frame1 .74/.76, frame5 1.34/1.35, overview12 2.63/2.36, overview48 9.13/8.38, inspect8 2.13/2.09.
Rejected: fixed -threads 1 (short frame1 .73->1.57, long GOP single frame), fixed 2 (short overview48 10.23 vs 9.30 in one round), -filter_threads 1 (no gain).
Retry redundancy: not simplified; no behavior evidence that any attempt is unneeded (RECENT bounds encode cost, Infinity covers sparse VFR, origin fallback + window 0 for AVI/TS kept).
Risk: -fps_mode needs FFmpeg 5.0+ for frame/overview/inspect (changes already requires 5.1; no version check on extraction).
close_reason: Reviewed passthrough synchronization fix with independently decoded expected/neighbor pixel evidence at 0.266, 7.125 and 7.25s. VFR and seek suite 12/12 pass. Measured bounded decoder thread allocation, retained origin retries; final benchmark validates uncontended speed.

title: Remove redundant image probing and bound concurrent sheet rendering
description: Own sheets module plus new test/sheets-output.test.js. Infer exact scaled image dimensions using same display/crop/aspect/even-rounding contract instead of ffprobe each first JPEG. Render independent sheets with modest bounded concurrency and deterministic order/window assignment; tune filters/encoder threads by measurements so parallel sheets do not oversubscribe. Preserve labels/size budget/small tile omission/SAR/crop/rotation and cancellation cleanup. Prefer existing tests; meaningful output dimensions and labels on generated/real video only.
acceptance_criteria: No image ffprobe needed; deterministic sheets and per-window manifest mapping; existing layout/label/dimension tests and real-video output pass.
notes:
Implemented (sheets.js + test/sheets-output.test.js only).
- frameSize({width,info,crop}) exported: replays FFmpeg scale=W:max(2,round(W/dar/2)*2) double arithmetic; dar=(w/h)*SAR on crop or displayed size. For 90/270 turns recovers exact den/num from probe's 1/(num/den) (continued fraction; verified 0/1e6 mismatches for n,d<=1000). Image ffprobe removed (~70-115ms per sheet run).
- buildSheets names all sheets in plan order and pushes to produced first, renders via shared pool(plans, 2), then assigns window.sheets and returns entries in plan order. Labels/budget/layout unchanged.
- Tests (3, real generated video): inferred size == extracted JPEG for ULP-order case 84x150@70->124, exact tie 128x90@64, SAR 2/1,1/2, crop, rotated SAR 12/11 @99 (inversion ULP case), rotated SAR crop; per-window color check on 5 concurrent sheets + manifest/disk order + sheet dims = cols*tile; fake ffmpeg parks sheet renders: exactly 2 concurrent of 4, SIGTERM -> 143, children dead, output removed. Mutations (no SAR recovery, exact arithmetic, jobs=3, reversed order) each fail one test.
- Indicative sheet-only timings (load avg 30-50, 1080p 640w frames, median of 5): o48 jobs1 1.87s / jobs2 0.78 / jobs4 0.77; i100 2.65/1.33/1.23; w10(10 sheets) 2.30/0.95/0.35. Default encoder threads (no -threads:v 1) and -filter_threads 1 showed no consistent gain; kept -threads:v 1, jobs=2.
- Full suite 84/84 pass.
close_reason: Reviewed removal of JPEG ffprobe, exact SAR/aspect/even rounding and bounded two-sheet pool with deterministic window mapping. Generated-video dimensions, sheet color/order, concurrency and cancellation coverage passed; final idle benchmark remains gated by agvid-aoh.9.

title: Simplify fail-fast output ownership while preserving private staging and cleanup
description: Own output module plus new test/output-ownership.test.js; existing output-related tests may be adjusted for deliberate contract change, coordinate ownership names. Replace hard-link publication/reclaim guards/automatic stale recovery/legacy guards with simple exclusive ownership (wx lock or equivalent), fail-fast existing lock with manual cleanup guidance. Preserve new-or-empty explicit output dirs and unique atomic default run dirs, private per-run staging, safe cancellation/failed cleanup, no deletion of other run files, simultaneous run exclusion, parent-directory cleanup. Stale output recovery deliberately becomes manual. Existing old automatic-recovery tests must be replaced by meaningful fail-fast and concurrent real CLI behavior tests, not merely removed silently. Do not edit CLI integration or docs.
acceptance_criteria: Simple ownership implementation; concurrent run and failure/signal cleanup real-video coverage; stale locks never stolen automatically; no overwritten user files.
notes: Impl (Opus subagent): src/output.js claim = open(lock,'wx') + pid/host; EEXIST -> inUse error naming holder pid/host and advising manual delete of .agvid.lock and .agvid.lock.work-*; no reclaim/guard/hard-link/staleness code. Work dirs never deleted by prefix; explicit dir with only leftover .agvid.lock.work-* -> 'holds work left by a killed agvid run' error listing names; other entries -> 'not empty'. Default run dir removed if claim errors. APIs outputDirectory/release/saveManifest/nonempty unchanged; cli.js untouched. Tests: test/cli.test.js reclaim tests (5 hook-based + empty-lock + reclaim-by-one + orphan) replaced by 2 real-CLI tests (dead/live/foreign/empty locks all refused, unchanged; after manual rm 1 of 4 concurrent runs owns; SIGKILLed run kept until manual clear, orphan FFmpeg cannot write into next run). New test/output-ownership.test.js: agvid-named user entries never deleted; killed default run untouched while SIGINT run cleans up and next run gets test-frame-1. Full suite 84/84 pass (node 24). Docs (README/skill/HELP) still describe auto reclaim? -> doc worker agvid-aoh.8.
close_reason: Reviewed exclusive wx ownership, refusal of every existing lock, preservation of arbitrary prefix-matching files, private staging and cleanup. Worker reports dedicated and full real-video suite pass (84 tests). Manual stale-lock cleanup is intentional and documented by agvid-aoh.8.

title: Split CLI into plain modules with independent implementation ownership
description: Own src/cli.js and new functional modules plus existing tests only if imports require it. Preserve behavior. Separate media probing/seeking/extraction, change detection, sheets, output ownership, child-process lifecycle/pool, argument validation/planning, and time/geometry helpers. Avoid cycles and architecture abstractions. Retain named CLI test exports by re-export if necessary. Establish media.extractFrames API used by CLI with current pooled extraction behavior, so future batching is confined to media module; sheets API owns dimension inference and sheet scheduling. Planning module owns source-independent validation and source-dependent planning; CLI owns output acquisition/detection/result summary integration. Do not touch benchmark scripts, docs or package.json. Report exact ownership map and exported interfaces. Current 83 tests must pass.
acceptance_criteria: Existing behavioral suite passes unchanged; module seams allow media, output and sheets independent edits; CLI becomes orchestration; timestamp/format/crop guarantees retained.
notes:
Split done (structural, no behavior change). Modules: cli.js (HELP, main, execute orchestration, test re-exports), plan.js (OPTIONS/parseArgs(args,help), videoStreamOption, resolveRange, planRun(command,options,info)->{crop,width,range?,times?,windows?,settings?}), probe.js (probe), media.js (extractFrames), changes.js (findChanges->{events,detection}), sheets.js (buildSheets, layout/labels), output.js (outputDirectory, release, saveManifest, nonempty), process.js (cancel/cancelled/cancellationError/start/run/lines/pool), seek.js (SOURCE_FORMAT, TICK, ORIGIN_MARGIN, TIME_TOLERANCE, attempts, seekArgs, trimEnd), time.js, geometry.js.
